description: Given a divine eye, Arjuna sees the Lord's sovereign form: many mouths and eyes, divine ornaments, garlands and raised weapons, facing every way (11.10–11); the whole world, divided in many ways, standing as one in the body of the god of gods (11.13); the gods, all kinds of beings, Brahmā on the lotus, the seers and divine serpents within it (11.15); no end, middle or beginning (11.16); crowned, with mace and discus, a mass of splendour hard to look at (11.17); sun and moon as eyes, mouth a blazing fire (11.19); the gods entering it and praising it (11.21–22); the warriors of both armies rushing into its tusked mouths and crushed between its teeth (11.26–30).
Because the Lord cannot be seen with one's own eye, he gives Arjuna a divine eye (divya cakṣus) with which to behold his sovereign yoga (11.8).

The radiance of the form is likened to that of a thousand suns rising at once in the sky (11.12); it is a mass of splendour blazing on every side with the brilliance of fire and sun, hard to look at (11.17), heating the universe (11.19), filling the world with fierce rays (11.30), 'made of splendour' (11.47).

On seeing the form Arjuna is overcome with amazement and his hair stands on end; he bows his head and speaks with joined palms (11.14); later he says he is thrilled (hṛṣita) at seeing what was never seen before, while his manas is shaken with fear (11.45).

Seeing the terrible form the worlds tremble and so does Arjuna (11.20, 11.23); shaken in his inmost being he finds neither steadiness nor calm (11.24), loses his bearings and finds no shelter, and begs the Lord to be gracious (11.25); he trembles and stammers in great fear (11.35); his manas is shaken with fear and he asks to see the former form (11.45–46). The Lord bids him not be distressed or bewildered and to be free of fear (11.49), and consoles him by resuming his gentle form (11.50).
When the Lord resumes his gentle, human form and consoles him, Arjuna says he has become composed, with cetas regained (sacetāḥ), and has returned to his natural state (prakṛti) (11.50–51).
